name: progress-bar
title: Progress bar
description: How far through something a player is, as a bar. Determinate is `data-gs-value` over `data-gs-max`; indeterminate is `data-gs-indeterminate` with no value and no aria-valuenow, so a screen reader hears "in progress" rather than nothing; zero is a real state that renders as one rather than an empty bar that looks broken; complete is `data-gs-complete`. There is no `data-gs-progress` and no `data-gs-fill`: CSS cannot divide one attribute by another, so the fraction the fill geometry needs is the custom property `--gs-progress`, a variable and not an attribute. The fill runs over the fill motion token and stops dead under reduced motion, so completion also changes the fill's colour, the track's edge and a glyph, which are emphasis and survive. Performs nothing: the host owns the number and says when it is finished.
docs: Pass `value` with `max` for a known fraction and `indeterminate` when there is none; a value passed alongside `indeterminate` is ignored rather than rendered, because a bar that is both 40% and unknowable is neither. Pass `min` when the floor is not zero, and it is omitted from the DOM when it is. Pass `complete` when the host says the thing is finished; the component never infers it from the number. Pass `format` to render the figure as something other than the bare number, and `data-gs-value` still carries the real one. `showLabel` puts the name and the figure above the track. BDS-022 makes this the base for `milestones` and `quest`, and `progressFraction` is exported so both compute the fraction the same way.
